summary: Create on-demand team bootstrap gateway: scoped service accounts, expiring Slack bot roles, and archival hooks
description:
Issue summary:
We need an automated 'team bootstrap gateway' that creates a new Jira project scaffold, Confluence space, Slack channel, and a minimal set of scoped service accounts/bot roles for short-lived experiments or external partner pods. The gateway must enforce timebound credentials (automatic expiry), include audit hooks that log who requested what, and wire in archival/retention policies for the created artifacts.

Background & why:
- Multiple pods request ad-hoc project sandboxes weekly; ops manually creates projects, channels, and service accounts which is error-prone and slow.
- Recent audits flagged gaps in ephemeral credential revocation and inconsistent Confluence space templates.
- We want a single, auditable flow that reduces toil while keeping security guardrails.

Request details & requirements:
1) Single webhook/API endpoint (AuthZ via Okta group) to trigger bootstrap. Input: team name, owner, duration (1d-90d), template choice (dev, experiment, partner).
2) Creates: Jira project (with standardized permission scheme), Confluence space (templated with onboarding checklist), Slack channel (#team-<name>-sandbox private), scoped service account(s) with least privilege and explicit TTL, and a Slack bot role scoped to the channel.
3) Automatic revocation job that runs at TTL expiry: removes service account keys, deactivates bot role, archives Slack channel, and sets Confluence space to read-only then archived after 30 days.
4) Audit logs forwarded to central logging (ELK) with requestor, timestamp, actions, and linked ticket key.
5) Admin UI in console to list active bootstraps, extend TTL once with approval, and force-terminate. Approvals should be implemented via a lightweight JIRA approval task to the owner's manager.
6) Tests & acceptance criteria (see below).

Security considerations:
- All service accounts created must use short-lived credentials (where possible exchange for federated tokens).
- No creation of high-privilege project roles in the bootstrap; only template-limited roles allowed.
- Record Okta actor, IP, and justification as part of the audit record.

Acceptance criteria/Test steps:
- Provision a sandbox for 'ml-eval-experiment' for 7 days: verify Jira project created with template, Confluence space present with checklist, Slack channel created and private, service account created with TTL set and token not reusable after expiry.
- Attempt to escalate permissions via Jira project admin UI should be blocked unless done through a separate org-level admin flow.
- After TTL expiry run: confirm service account tokens revoked, Slack channel archived, Confluence space set to read-only, and entry in ELK shows the lifecycle events.
- Admin UI shows the bootstrap and allows one extension after manager approval, otherwise shows queued archival.

Proposed rollout plan:
- Design & implementation (2 sprints): API + workflow + templates.
- Internal beta with one pod for 2 weeks.
- Audit and iterate based on beta.

Notes on dependencies:
- Okta group for requesters must exist (ops/grant-team-bootstrap).
- Slack bot provisioning API permissions (we may need an elevated bot for channel-scoped role assignment).
- Confluence template created and canonicalized (link above).
